title: Global Climate Goals in Danger as Temperatures Rise and Funding Stalls
subtitle: New data shows 2026 is on track to be one of the hottest years ever, while support for developing nations remains stuck.

summary.en: Global temperatures are expected to stay above the 1.5-degree limit in 2026. This trend makes the goals of the Paris Agreement harder to reach. Meanwhile, developing nations are not receiving the financial help they were promised. Wealthy countries are failing to provide the money needed for climate adaptation. Experts warn that the world is moving toward a future that will be very difficult to manage.
summary.zh: 全球氣溫預計在二〇二六年將持續高於一點五度的限制。此趨勢使得《巴黎協定》的目標更難達成。與此同時，開發中國家並未獲得承諾的財務援助。富裕國家未能提供氣候調適所需的資金。專家警告，世界正走向一個極難駕馭的未來。

paragraphs.en: The world is facing a double crisis as temperatures continue to climb and international efforts to fund climate protection lose momentum. According to the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service, 2026 is almost certain to be the second-warmest year on record. This follows a trend of rising heat that has pushed global temperatures above the 1.5-degree Celsius threshold set by the 2015 Paris Agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 全球正面臨雙重危機，氣溫持續攀升，而國際間為氣候保護提供資金的努力卻後繼無力。根據歐盟的哥白尼氣候變化服務（Copernicus Climate Change Service），二〇二六年幾乎確定會成為有紀錄以來第二熱的一年。這延續了氣溫升高的趨勢，已將全球氣溫推升至二〇一五年《巴黎協定》所設定的攝氏一點五度門檻之上。

paragraphs.en: The Paris Agreement was a major global deal aimed at keeping long-term temperature increases well below 2 degrees Celsius, with a preference for staying under 1.5 degrees. However, the latest data shows that the planet is struggling to meet these targets. October 2026 was the warmest October ever recorded, marking the third month in a row where temperatures stayed above the 1.5-degree limit. Samantha Burgess of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts noted that an exceptionally strong El Nino—a natural weather pattern that brings warmer ocean temperatures—is adding more heat to a planet already warming because of human activities.
paragraphs.zh: 《巴黎協定》是一項重要的全球協議，旨在將長期氣溫升幅控制在攝氏兩度以內，並以維持在一點五度以下為目標。然而，最新數據顯示地球正難以達成這些目標。二〇二六年十月是有紀錄以來最熱的十月，這也是氣溫連續第三個月維持在一點五度的限制之上。歐洲中期天氣預報中心（European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts）的伯吉斯（Samantha Burgess）指出，異常強烈的聖嬰現象——一種帶來海洋高溫的自然天氣型態——正為一個因人類活動而持續暖化的地球增添更多熱能。

paragraphs.en: While the climate continues to change, the financial support needed to handle these shifts is failing to grow. Recent reports from the United Nations show that funding for "adaptation"—the process of changing how we live and build to survive extreme weather—has stopped increasing. Wealthy nations have long promised to provide financial help to developing countries, which are often the most affected by climate disasters. However, these promises are currently not being met, leaving many nations without the resources to protect their people from floods, droughts, and heatwaves.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管氣候持續變遷，但應對這些轉變所需的財務支援卻未能增加。聯合國近期的報告顯示，用於「調適」——即改變生活與建設方式以在極端天氣下生存的過程——的資金已停止成長。富裕國家長期以來承諾向開發中國家提供財務援助，而這些國家往往是氣候災難受創最深的地區。然而，這些承諾目前並未兌現，導致許多國家缺乏資源來保護人民免受洪水、乾旱與熱浪的侵襲。

paragraphs.en: The situation is becoming increasingly urgent. The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) now expects that global warming will go beyond the 1.5-degree target. While a single year above this level does not mean the Paris Agreement has failed, the trend is clear. Johan Rockström, a climate scientist at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, warned that humanity is currently on a path toward an "unmanageable future." He explained that every small increase in temperature makes the risks to the planet much worse.
paragraphs.zh: 情勢正變得日益緊迫。聯合國環境規劃署（UNEP）目前預期全球暖化將會超越一點五度的目標。雖然單一年份超過此水準並不代表《巴黎協定》已經失敗，但趨勢已相當明確。波茨坦氣候影響研究中心（Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research）的氣候科學家洛克斯特倫（Johan Rockström）警告，人類目前正走向一個「難以駕馭的未來」。他解釋說，氣溫每升高一點點，對地球造成的風險就會嚴重許多。

paragraphs.en: To avoid the worst outcomes, experts suggest that the world must act quickly. The UNEP has created a plan where warming might reach 1.7 to 1.8 degrees by the middle of the century before falling back to 1.5 degrees by the year 2100. Achieving this, however, requires a massive change in how the world produces energy. It would mean cutting emissions—the gases released into the atmosphere that trap heat—by 69% by 2040. Rockström also emphasized that we must find ways to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to help lower temperatures again.
paragraphs.zh: 為了避免最壞的結果，專家建議全球必須迅速採取行動。聯合國環境規劃署制定了一項計畫，預測暖化程度可能在本世紀中葉達到一點七至一點八度，隨後在二一〇〇年降回一點五度。然而，要達成此目標，需要全球能源生產方式進行大規模的轉變。這意味著必須在二〇四〇年之前，將排放量——即釋放到大氣中並鎖住熱能的氣體——減少百分之六十九。洛克斯特倫也強調，我們必須找到從大氣中移除二氧化碳的方法，以協助降低氣溫。

paragraphs.en: For many developing nations, the lack of funding is a major barrier to these goals. Without the money promised by wealthier countries, these nations cannot build the infrastructure needed to transition to cleaner energy or protect their citizens from the impacts of a warming world. The failure to provide this support creates a divide in the global response to climate change. While some countries are investing in new technology, others are left to face the consequences of a changing climate with very little help.
paragraphs.zh: 對於許多開發中國家而言，資金匱乏是達成這些目標的主要障礙。若沒有富裕國家承諾的資金，這些國家便無法建立轉型至潔淨能源所需的基礎設施，也無法保護國民免受暖化世界的衝擊。未能提供這些支援，在應對氣候變遷的全球行動中造成了分歧。當部分國家正投資於新技術時，其他國家卻只能在幾乎沒有協助的情況下，獨自面對氣候變遷帶來的後果。

paragraphs.en: The outlook for the coming years remains difficult. As the world moves toward a period of higher temperatures, the need for both emissions cuts and financial support for vulnerable nations has never been higher. The UN reports suggest that the world must keep the "overshoot"—the time spent above the 1.5-degree limit—as short as possible to avoid dangerous tipping points. These are moments when the climate system changes in ways that are impossible to reverse. Whether the international community can come together to provide the necessary funding and reach these ambitious emissions targets remains the most important question for the years ahead.
paragraphs.zh: 未來幾年的前景依然艱困。隨著全球邁向高溫時期，對於減少排放以及為脆弱國家提供財務支援的需求，從未如此迫切。聯合國報告建議，全球必須將「超標」——即氣溫高於一點五度限制的時間——縮減至最短，以避免危險的臨界點。這些臨界點是指氣候系統發生無法逆轉的變化時刻。國際社會能否團結一致提供必要資金並達成這些雄心勃勃的減排目標，仍是未來幾年最重要的課題。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become less effective, active, or successful over time.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡的 momentum 指的是進展的勢頭。文中：international efforts to fund climate protection lose momentum.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Known or documented in official history.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於氣候或統計數據，指被正式記錄下來的數據。文中：2026 is almost certain to be the second-warmest year on record.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To decrease or return to a lower level after being higher.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指氣溫數值從高點下降。文中：warming might reach 1.7 to 1.8 degrees by the middle of the century before falling back to 1.5 degrees by the year 2100.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A critical moment when a small change causes a large, often irreversible, shift in a system.
keyTerms.noteZh: 在氣候科學中指不可逆轉的關鍵轉折點。文中：These are moments when the climate system changes in ways that are impossible to reverse.

previousArticles.title: Climate Funding for Poorer Nations Stalls as Needs Grow
previousArticles.summaryEn: A new United Nations report shows that money to help developing countries deal with climate change has stopped growing. Wealthy nations are not meeting their promises to provide enough financial support for adaptation. Developing countries need billions of dollars to protect themselves from floods, heatwaves, and rising sea levels. Many poor nations are suffering the most despite contributing the least to global warming. Experts warn that failing to act now will make future costs much higher and put millions of people at risk.

previousArticles.title: Global Climate Funding Stalls as Needs for Poorer Nations Grow
previousArticles.summaryEn: A recent United Nations report shows that financial aid for climate adaptation in developing nations has stopped growing. Wealthy countries are failing to meet their promises to help poorer nations prepare for extreme weather. Developing countries face a massive gap between the money they need and the funding they actually receive. The situation is especially difficult for the world's poorest nations and small island states. Experts warn that failing to provide this support will lead to higher costs and greater human suffering in the future.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the specific target for reducing emissions by 2040 to help keep warming under control?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，為了在世紀中葉將暖化控制在 1.7 到 1.8 度並在 2100 年降回 1.5 度，必須在 2040 年前將排放量減少 69%。選項 A 與 D 混淆了溫度目標與排放削減比例，選項 C 則是誤將溫度預測數值當作削減目標，均不正確。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between wealthy nations and developing nations regarding climate change?

options.A: Wealthy nations are successfully leading the transition to cleaner energy for all countries.
options.B: Developing nations have refused financial help from wealthy nations to maintain their independence.
options.C: The lack of promised financial support from wealthy nations hinders the ability of developing nations to adapt.
options.D: Developing nations are currently contributing more to the 'overshoot' than wealthy nations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三段與第六段，富裕國家承諾提供資金援助但未兌現，導致開發中國家缺乏資源來適應極端氣候或轉型清潔能源。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 文中未提及拒絕援助；選項 D 則無證據顯示開發中國家是造成超標的主因，故選 C。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'overshoot' refer to in the context of the 1.5-degree limit?

options.A: The period of time during which temperatures exceed the established safety threshold.
options.B: The act of setting climate goals that are too difficult to achieve.
options.C: The sudden drop in global temperatures after a long period of warming.
options.D: The failure of international organizations to reach a consensus on climate policy.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到「overshoot」是指氣溫超過 1.5 度限制的這段時間。選項 B、C、D 皆未準確反映文中對該詞彙的定義，文中強調的是必須盡量縮短氣溫高於限制的時間，以避免不可逆的氣候臨界點。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: El Nino is the sole cause of the recent rise in global temperatures.
options.B: The Paris Agreement has successfully kept global warming below 1.5 degrees.
options.C: Technological advancements alone will be enough to reverse climate change by 2100.
options.D: Urgent action in emission cuts and financial support is needed to address the growing climate crisis.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文的核心在於探討全球暖化危機加劇，並強調解決此問題需要兩大支柱：一是大幅削減排放量，二是富裕國家必須履行對開發中國家的資金承諾。選項 A 過度簡化原因；選項 B 與文中提到的氣溫超標事實矛盾；選項 C 忽略了資金援助的重要性。
